summary.headline: KPI Green Q1 FY27 total income rose 16% YoY to INR710 crore and EBITDA 21% to INR262 crore, but PAT fell to INR95 crore from INR111 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue and EBITDA grew, with EBITDA margin up to 37% from 35%, but PAT declined as depreciation and interest on newly commissioned IPP assets were booked upfront while revenue ramps. Management said billing delays on utility-scale EPC projects pushed revenue into the next quarter, and cited geopolitical cost pressure on steel, cables, logistics and cranes. Portfolio reached 6.94 GW (1.87 GW installed, 5.07 GW WIP). Management guided to 30-40% revenue growth (softened from the chairman's 40-50%) and a PAT margin below the earlier 16-18% for FY27. The CFO Salim Yahoo is leaving and Kapil Kriplani joins as Group CFO.

segments.name: IPP (Independent Power Producer)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 2.57 GW; expected to generate more than 390 crore units annually at full run rate; management cites 85-90% EBITDA margin on IPP and 25-year PPAs. Management expects IPP revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW is at peak, with peak timing in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: CPP (Captive Power Producer) / EPC
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 4.37 GW; CPP order book approximately INR5,000-plus crore. Management said EPC is about 83% of total revenue, and that margins were hit by higher costs for steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes.

segments.name: Sun Drops Energia (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management expects Sun Drops to cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in FY27 across IPP and CPP; Sun Drops IPO is mentioned as upcoming.

segments.name: KP Energy (EPC subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Per analyst, EBITDA margin fell from 22% to 12%; management attributed it to a pure EPC model with greater exposure to cost inflation and shared-cost absorption.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 30-40% YoY for FY27, with management saying it is being conservative given geopolitical conditions; chairman had earlier spoken of 40-50%.
PAT margin for FY27 expected to be below the earlier 16-18% guidance; no specific revised number given.
Management expects the full earning contribution of new IPP assets to build through the rest of FY27, with most projects targeted for energization by September and full stabilisation in FY28.
Long-term debt to net worth targeted at a maximum of 3:1; management said leverage could rise to around 3x as project loans are drawn.

Annual interest cost for the full IPP capacity estimated at around INR450 crore (at about 8.5%); IPP depreciation estimated at about 5% on the building component, with total IPP capex potentially INR5,000-6,000 crore in FY27-28.
Botswana: 500 MW first phase under planning; management said no revenue from Botswana in FY27, with revenue in later years.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 6.94 GW as of June 30, 2026 (up 71% YoY from 4.06 GW): 1.87 GW installed plus 5.07 GW work in progress.
Commissioned 0.85 GW and booked 2.88 GW of fresh orders over the year.
Land bank 8,657 acres; power evacuation capacity 5.10 GW; 133 sites total after entering Rajasthan.
BESS: 565 MW / 1,130 MWh project executed, financial closure under process.
Floating solar: 142 MW EPC order at Kadana Dam, Gujarat under execution.
150 MW wind for GUVNL: PPA signed and financial closure achieved; 300 MW SJVN-backed wind PPA signing under process.
Botswana: MoU with government for 5 GW; 500 hectares of land acquired (transcript corrected from 500 acres); PPAs at an advanced stage.
Energy trading licences from GERC (intrastate) and CERC (interstate); trading in pilot mode.
UAE: solar plus BESS project for a containerised data centre awarded to subsidiary Sun Drops Energia, under execution.
demand_pricing: Management said data centres are an emerging opportunity with inquiries ongoing, but no order share was quantified.
Growth slowed below guidance because utility-scale billing for customers such as Coal India, Adani Group and Aditya Birla Group slipped into Q2.

Geopolitical conditions raised costs of steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes; management said costs were partly absorbed and partly passed on to customers, and that sales were not affected.
Inventory built up at end-March to secure materials amid geopolitical disruption; it fell somewhat in Q1 and is expected to decline further as projects complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why was execution slow versus guidance, with growth of 16% against the 40-50% previously cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall was billing timing on utility-scale projects, and that it is now guiding to 30-40% growth, being conservative due to geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the sharp fall in CPP and KP Energy gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed higher balance-of-plant, logistics and cost inflation from geopolitical conditions; KP Energy is pure EPC with about 17-18% of its revenue from IPP, so it was more exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Will IPP stay at a share of the revenue mix, and is the balance sheet strained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep IPP at about 20-odd% of revenue mix; leverage is 'below 3' and may rise towards 3x as loans for projects due by September are drawn, with EPS expected to recover as plants stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the annual interest cost, EBITDA and depreciation for the IPP business at full scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest is around INR450 crore a year at about 8.5% on roughly INR5,000 crore of debt; IPP EBITDA is 85-90% with revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW peaks, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27; depreciation is about 5% on the building component.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 PAT margin meet the 16-18% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 and Q4 would recover only part of the Q1-Q2 gap, so the FY27 PAT margin would be lower than 16-18%; full benefit is expected in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 cash flow from operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Salim Yahoo estimated about INR140-150 crore, computed as PAT of about INR94 crore plus quarterly depreciation of about INR45 crore.
